name: gasoline_engine_excess_air_exhaust_analysis
title: Gasoline engine: excess air and useful power from exhaust-gas analysis
summary: Combustion of gasoline (CH1.95) with excess air in an engine, analysed from the dry exhaust-gas CO mole fraction (incomplete combustion); the excess air follows from the fuel-air ratio and the useful power from the five-box energy balance, with the fuel vaporised at the reference state (its LHV is defined for gaseous fuel).

authors: S. Borguet (ULiège, per the collection inventory)

verification.summary: Not the native file but its runnable variant was compared with the EES stored solution of THD10_R11_E2.EES: 54 common variables, 6 differ (rtol=0.001), all absolute-Air-enthalpy reference offsets or ideal-gas property differences <= 2.73e-03; e, lambda, far and Q_dot_utile agree within 2.6e-04.
verification.reference: EES stored solution of the source file (54 variables, --ees-units); the comparison concerns the runnable variant gasoline_engine_excess_air_exhaust_analysis_coolsolve.eescode, the native file being blocked
verification.notes: Native file: 'Unknown fluid: CarbonMonoxide' (CS-GAP-FLUIDS-ALIAS), square system otherwise (54/54). Variant vs EES: 6 of 54 variables differ above rtol=0.001 - h_a_ref/h_a_su (absolute Air enthalpy reference: EES 0 at 0 K vs CoolProp), h_N2_ex, q_N2 (1.24e-03), q_CO2 (2.73e-03), Q_dot_1 (1.71e-03, 0.4 W absolute) - ideal-gas EES-vs-CoolProp property differences within the 0.5 % tolerance. Key results: e 0.0471045 vs 0.0471167, lambda 104.7104 vs 104.7117 %, Q_dot_utile -83938.0 vs -83921.5 W.
